source: Order from the 2018 Turkish word list of FrequencyWords by Hermit Dave (CC BY-SA 4.0), built from the OpenSubtitles2018 corpus (opensubtitles.org, via OPUS; Lison, Tiedemann and Kouylekov 2018), so it reflects film and TV dialogue. Forms were lowercased and merged into lemmas with the zeyrek analyser (a Python port of Zemberek-NLP), forms that fit two lemmas were split in proportion to how common each lemma is, and the result was cleaned by hand: names, fragments and obscenities removed, some words turned into phrase or compound-verb cards. Ranks are estimates, not exact corpus counts. The ranked list is scripts/turkish/wordlist.tsv (CC BY-SA 4.0); method in turkish/PROJECT.md 7.8. Glosses, examples and notes are original.

ex.en: How much is this painting worth?

cards.note: *Değerli* = valuable. Not the same as *değer* from *değmek* (to be worth it): *Buna değer* = It's worth it.

en: to deal with, to work on

ex.en: I spent all day dealing with this job.

cards.note: Takes *-lA*: *bu işle uğraşmak*. *Benimle uğraşma!* = Don't mess with me! The noun *uğraş* is an effort or a pastime.

ex.tr: Annem için güzel bir hediye aldım.
ex.en: I bought a nice present for my mom.

cards.note: *Hediye etmek* = to give as a present; *doğum günü hediyesi* = birthday present.

ex.en: There are twenty students in the class.

cards.note: *Kaçıncı sınıftasın?* = What grade are you in? Also a category: *birinci sınıf* = first-class.

ex.en: Sorry I'm late.

cards.note: *Kusura bakma* (polite: *Kusura bakmayın*) = Sorry, excuse me; literally, don't look at the fault. *Kusursuz* = flawless.

ex.en: Everyone was very scared after the attack.

cards.note: From *saldırmak* (to attack). A heart attack is *kalp krizi*, not *saldırı*.

ex.tr: Şöyle yapalım: önce yiyelim, sonra gidelim.
ex.en: Let's do it like this: first we eat, then we go.

cards.note: *Şöyle* points to what comes next, *böyle* to what is here, *öyle* to what was said. *Şöyle böyle* = so-so.

en: captain (of a ship, a plane, a team)

ex.en: Our team's captain is Emre.

cards.note: The t doesn't soften: *kaptanı*. Of a ship, a plane or a team; the pilot in command of an airliner is the *kaptan pilot*.

ex.en: The children are playing ball in the garden.

cards.note: *Top oynamak* = to play ball; *futbol topu* = soccer ball. Not to be confused with *toplamak* (to collect).

ex.tr: Dün gece garip bir rüya gördüm.
ex.en: I had a strange dream last night.

cards.note: *Rüya görmek* = to dream, literally to see a dream: *Rüyamda seni gördüm*. A wish or ambition is *hayal*.

ex.en: This is a very quiet neighbourhood.

cards.note: *Ses* (sound, voice) + *-sIz* (without). *Sessiz ol!* = Be quiet! *Sessizce* = quietly.

en: to get off, to get out (of a vehicle)
to go down, to come down

ex.en: We're getting off at the next stop.

cards.note: What you get off or come down takes the ablative: *otobüsten inmek*, *merdivenden inmek*. A plane *iner* (lands). The opposite is *binmek*.

ex.en: See you soon!

cards.note: The locative of *yakın* (near), so also **nearby**: *yakında bir eczane* (a pharmacy nearby). With the future: *Yakında döneceğim*.

ex.en: There are big waves on the sea today.

cards.note: *Dalga geçmek* (colloquial) = to make fun of, to fool around: *Benimle dalga mı geçiyorsun?* = Are you kidding me?

ex.en: The thief spent three years in prison.

cards.note: The i drops before a vowel: *hapse girmek* (to go to prison), but *hapisten çıkmak*. *Hapis yatmak* = to serve time. The building is *hapishane* or *cezaevi*.

ex.en: What time will we get to Ankara?

cards.note: One of the 13 verbs with the aorist `-Ir`: *varır*. The place takes the dative: *eve varmak*. Not to be confused with *var* (there is).

ex.en: I only waited five minutes.

cards.note: A little more formal than *sadece*. *Yalnız* also means **only**, as well as **alone** and **but**.

ex.tr: Bu ilacı günde iki kez iç.
ex.en: Take this medicine twice a day.

cards.note: The ç becomes c before a vowel: *ilacı*. Medicine is taken with *içmek* or *almak*. *Böcek ilacı* = insecticide; illegal drugs are *uyuşturucu*.

ex.tr: Bu kısım çok önemli, dikkatli okuyun.
ex.en: This part is very important, read it carefully.

cards.note: The ı drops before a vowel: *kısmı*, *kısmen* (partly). *Bölüm* is a chapter or an episode.

ex.en: I left my bag on the bus.

cards.note: *Okul çantası* = school bag, *el çantası* = handbag, *sırt çantası* = backpack.

ex.en: Birds fly south in winter.

cards.note: Planes and birds *uçar*; people usually *uçakla gider* (go by plane). *Uçak* (plane) and *uçuş* (flight) come from it.

en: to swear, to take an oath

ex.tr: Yemin ederim, ben bir şey yapmadım!
ex.en: I swear, I didn't do anything!

cards.note: *Yemin ederim!* = I swear! The noun is *yemin* (oath). Swearing in the sense of cursing is *küfür etmek*.

ex.en: Did you see the expression on his face?

cards.note: *İfade etmek* = to express; *ifade vermek* = to give a statement. *Yüz ifadesi* = facial expression.

ex.en: In summer we go swimming in the sea every day.

cards.note: *Denize girmek* = to go swimming in the sea; *deniz kenarı* = seaside. *Karadeniz* = the Black Sea, *Akdeniz* = the Mediterranean.

ex.en: Can I pay by card?

cards.note: A bank card, a greeting card or a game card: *kredi kartı* (credit card), *doğum günü kartı*. A business card is a *kartvizit*.

ex.en: Exercise is good for the body.

cards.note: The t becomes d before a vowel: *vücudu*. A living body; a dead one is *ceset*. *Beden* is a synonym, and also a clothing size.

ex.en: This heat is like hell!

cards.note: The opposite is *cennet* (paradise, heaven). *Cehenneme git!* = Go to hell! (rude).

ex.en: Life in the city is very expensive.

cards.note: From *yaşamak* (to live). *Hayat* is more common in speech; *yaşam* is preferred in compounds such as *yaşam tarzı* (lifestyle).

en: to drop by, to stop by
to suffer, to undergo (an attack, a loss)

ex.en: I'll drop by your place this evening.

cards.note: The place takes the dative: *markete uğramak*. The a becomes u before `-(I)yor`: *uğruyor*. Also *saldırıya uğramak* = to be attacked.

en: concern, care (umurumda değil: I don't care)

ex.en: I don't care about money.

cards.note: Almost only with a possessive and *değil* or a question: *umurumda değil* (I don't care), *Umurunda mı?* (Does he care?). The thing cared about is the subject. Colloquial.

ex.en: We have no evidence.

cards.note: The t doesn't soften: *kanıtı*. *Kanıtlamak* = to prove. *Delil* is a more formal synonym.

ex.en: Do you have plans this evening?

cards.note: *Programın var mı?* = Are you free? Do you have plans? *Program yapmak* = to make plans.

ex.en: Did you like the movie?

cards.note: For things you see, try or taste, with the accusative: *Elbiseyi beğendim*. *Sevmek* is for lasting likes and for love.

ex.en: What's in this box?

cards.note: Also a can: *bir kutu kola*. *Posta kutusu* = mailbox.

ex.tr: Bu karar büyük bir sorun yarattı.
ex.en: This decision created a big problem.

cards.note: *Yaratıcı* = creative; *yaratık* = creature. Making something with your hands is *yapmak*.

ex.en: What is your date of birth?

cards.note: From *doğmak* (to be born). *Doğum günü* = birthday; *doğum yeri* = place of birth.

ex.tr: Bu konuya dair hiçbir bilgim yok.
ex.en: I have no information about this matter.

cards.note: After the dative, and rather formal: *buna dair*. Speech uses *hakkında* or *ile ilgili*. Not to be confused with *daire* (apartment).

ex.en: Today is my lucky day!

cards.note: *Şans* (luck) + *-lI*. The opposite is *şanssız* (unlucky).

ex.en: Is this museum open to the public?

cards.note: *Halk müziği* = folk music, *halk dansları* = folk dances. *Halka açık* = open to the public.

ex.en: It's a secret, don't tell anyone!

cards.note: The r doubles before a vowel: *sırrı*, *sırrım*. *Sır tutmak* = to keep a secret; *gizli* = secret (adjective).

ex.en: Shall we have fish tonight?

cards.note: The k becomes ğ before a vowel: *balığı*. *Balık tutmak* = to fish; *balıkçı* = fisherman or fish restaurant.

ex.en: It's very hot today.

cards.note: For the weather, food, drinks and people (*sıcak bir insan*, a warm person). For **I'm hot**, say *Sıcakladım*.

ex.tr: Evin yakınında güzel bir park var.
ex.en: There's a nice park near the house.

cards.note: Also parking: *park etmek* (to park), *otopark* (parking lot), *Park yapılmaz* (no parking).

ex.tr: Eskiden düşmandık, şimdi en iyi arkadaşız.
ex.en: We used to be enemies, now we're best friends.

cards.note: *Düşmanlık* = hostility. A rival in sports or business is *rakip*.

ex.en: He tied the dog to the tree.

cards.note: The a becomes ı before `-(I)yor`: *bağlıyor*. On the phone: *Sizi müdüre bağlıyorum* (I'm putting you through to the manager). *Bağlı* = tied; connected.

ex.en: I left the shopping list at home.

cards.note: *Alışveriş listesi* = shopping list; *bekleme listesi* = waiting list.

ex.en: I wrote a long letter to my mom.

cards.note: The p becomes b before a vowel: *mektubu*. A letter of the alphabet is *harf*.

ex.en: I set up an appointment for you.

cards.note: The a becomes ı before `-(I)yor`: *ayarlıyor*. From *ayar* (setting): *saati ayarlamak* = to set a clock.

ex.en: Are the glasses clean?

cards.note: *Temizlemek* = to clean; *tertemiz* = spotlessly clean; *temiz hava* = fresh air.

ex.en: The doctor asked for a blood test.

cards.note: A medical test (*kan testi*, *hamilelik testi*) or a multiple-choice test; a school exam is usually *sınav*.

ex.en: Sleep is very important for the brain.

cards.note: The i drops before a vowel: *beyni*. *Beyin fırtınası* = brainstorming. The mind is *akıl*.

ex.en: Excuse me, where's the station?

cards.note: From French. For getting attention or a small apology; a real apology is *özür dilerim*. *Pardon?* also asks someone to repeat.

ex.en: The danger is over, we can come out now.

cards.note: *Tehlikeli* = dangerous; *tehlikede* = in danger.

ex.en: I don't think that man is guilty.

cards.note: *Suç* (crime, fault) + *-lI*. The opposite is *suçsuz* or *masum* (innocent). *Kendini suçlu hissetmek* = to feel guilty.

ex.en: We moved here two years ago.

cards.note: Means the same as *yıl*, and is a little more colloquial. *Seneye* = next year, *geçen sene* = last year.

ex.en: I wish you'd come too.

cards.note: With the conditional `-sA` for a wish (*Keşke gelsen*), with `-sAydI` for a regret (*Keşke gelseydin*: I wish you had come).

en: to suit, to fit, to match

ex.tr: Yarın saat beş sana uyar mı?
ex.en: Does five o'clock tomorrow suit you?

cards.note: What is suited or obeyed takes the dative: *kurallara uymak* (to follow the rules). *Uyuyor* is also the present of *uyumak* (to sleep).

ex.en: This road is very dangerous at night.

cards.note: *Tehlike* (danger) + *-lI*. The opposite is *güvenli* (safe).

ex.en: Our hotel is very close to the sea.

cards.note: *Otelde kalmak* = to stay at a hotel. A small family hotel is a *pansiyon*.

ex.en: I spent a lot of money this month.

cards.note: The a becomes ı before `-(I)yor`: *harcıyor*. Spending time is usually *geçirmek*; *vakit harcamak* = to waste time.

en: to get caught, to get stuck

ex.en: I'm stuck in traffic, I'll be a bit late.

cards.note: The passive of *takmak* (to attach, to put on). *Bana takılma!* = Stop teasing me! In casual speech, *takılmak* is also to hang out.

ex.en: I can't see anything in the dark.

cards.note: The k becomes ğ before a vowel: *karanlığı*. Also an adjective: *karanlık bir oda*. *Hava karardı* = it got dark.

ex.en: The view was incredibly beautiful!

cards.note: Literally **that can't be believed**, from *inanmak*. Often an intensifier: *inanılmaz güzel*.

ex.en: This is a very simple question.

cards.note: Also **easy**: *basit bir iş*. Said of a person or an act, *basit* is a put-down: cheap, petty.

ex.en: Don't miss this opportunity!

cards.note: *Fırsat bulmak* = to find the time or the chance; *fırsat bu fırsat* = while we have the chance. Luck is *şans*.

ex.en: I grew up in a small town.

cards.note: Bigger than a *köy* (village), smaller than a *şehir* (city). Not to be confused with *kasap* (butcher).

ex.en: It's thirty degrees today.

cards.note: *Sıfırın altında beş derece* = five below zero. *Dereceye girmek* = to place in a race or an exam.

ex.en: The party was a lot of fun.

cards.note: *Eğlence* (fun, entertainment) + *-lI*; *eğlenmek* = to have fun. The opposite is *sıkıcı* (boring).

ex.en: The meal was wonderful, thank you!

cards.note: Stronger than *güzel* or *harika*: *muhteşem bir manzara* (a magnificent view).

ex.en: The detective finally found the killer.

cards.note: Common in novels and films; the police officer in charge of a case is usually a *komiser*.

ex.en: The police found drugs in the car.

cards.note: From *uyuşturmak* (to numb). Only illegal drugs; medicine is *ilaç*.

en: to take off, to take out

ex.en: Take your shoes off, please.

cards.note: Used like *çıkarmak*, which is the more standard form and the one the lessons teach. *Çıkartma* = sticker.

ex.en: This money isn't enough.

cards.note: From *yetmek* (to be enough): *Yeter!* = Enough! Stop it! *Yeterince* = enough (adverb).

ex.tr: Bu sokakta her yerde kamera var.
ex.en: There are cameras everywhere on this street.

cards.note: Usually a video or security camera; a camera for photos is a *fotoğraf makinesi*.

ex.en: Can you do me a favour?

cards.note: The k becomes ğ before a vowel: *iyiliği*. *İyilik yapmak* = to do a favour. *İyilik sağlık* = all good (a casual reply to *Nasılsın?*).

ex.en: This building is very old.

cards.note: Any building; a block of flats is an *apartman*. *Binanın kapısı* = the building's door.

ex.en: The meeting starts at three.

cards.note: From *toplanmak* (to gather). *Toplantıdayım* = I'm in a meeting.

ex.en: Why are you laughing?

cards.note: What you laugh at takes the dative: *Bana gülme!* (Don't laugh at me!). *Gülümsemek* means only to smile.

ex.en: The sun rises at seven.

cards.note: *Güneş doğuyor* = the sun is rising, *güneş batıyor* = it's setting. *Güneş gözlüğü* = sunglasses; *güneşli* = sunny.

ex.en: Will you teach me Turkish?

cards.note: The learner takes the dative: *Çocuklara matematik öğretiyor*. From *öğrenmek* (to learn); *öğretmen* = teacher.

ex.en: The neighbours are fighting again.

cards.note: *Kavga etmek* = to fight, to quarrel (with: *-lA*). A war is *savaş*; an argument is also a *tartışma*.

ex.en: I have to finish the report by tomorrow.

cards.note: Also a doctor's note for sick leave: *rapor almak*, *raporlu olmak* (to be on sick leave).

ex.en: My uncle lives in Izmir.

cards.note: The mother's brother is *dayı*. Children and young people call any older man *amca*: *Amca, saat kaç?*

ex.en: What nonsense!

cards.note: From *saçma* (absurd). *Saçmalama!* = Don't talk nonsense! Colloquial.

ex.en: I'll love you forever.

cards.note: *Son* (end) + *-sIz* (without). *Sonsuza kadar* = forever.

ex.en: We worked until morning.

cards.note: After the dative, like *kadar*: *akşama dek*. Mostly written or formal; speech uses *kadar*.

en: to be sad, to be upset

ex.en: I'm very sorry about this.

cards.note: The cause takes the dative: *Buna üzüldüm*. *Üzülme!* = Don't be sad, never mind. From *üzmek* (to upset).

ex.en: What shall we have for lunch?

cards.note: *Öğle yemeği* = lunch; *öğleden sonra* = afternoon. *Öğlen* (noon; at noon) is the everyday form.

ex.en: We're in trouble!

cards.note: *Başı belada* = in trouble; *bela çıkarmak* = to make trouble; *belalı* = troublesome; troublemaker.

ex.en: It'll probably rain tomorrow.

cards.note: One word, with â (TDK). *Galiba* and *muhtemelen* are close in meaning.

ex.en: The Ottoman army was very large.

cards.note: A soldier is *asker*, military service *askerlik*. *Ordu* is also a city on the Black Sea.

ex.en: Seriously? I can't believe it.

cards.note: *Cidden mi?* = Seriously? From *ciddi* (serious); close to *gerçekten*.

ex.en: The chef of this restaurant is very famous.

cards.note: A head cook or a boss: *şefim* (my boss). An ordinary cook is an *aşçı*.

ex.en: I have to go to court tomorrow.

cards.note: *Mahkemeye vermek* = to take to court. The judge is *hâkim* or *yargıç*; the case is a *dava*.

ex.en: These goods come from China.

cards.note: *Mal sahibi* = owner. In slang *mal* is an insult (idiot); best avoided.

ex.en: I write with my left hand.

cards.note: *Sola dönün* = turn left; *solda* = on the left. The opposite is *sağ*.

ex.en: The internet connection is very slow.

cards.note: From *bağlamak* (to tie, to connect). *Bağlantı kurmak* = to get in touch.

ex.en: There's a nice picture on the wall.

cards.note: A wall of a room or a building; a city wall is a *sur*.

ex.en: We watched the game live.

cards.note: *Can* (life, soul) + *-lI*. *Canlı yayın* = live broadcast, *canlı müzik* = live music. As a noun, a living thing.

ex.en: Respect for elders is very important.

cards.note: *Saygı duymak* = to respect (dative): *Ona saygı duyuyorum*. *Saygılarımla* = Yours sincerely, at the end of a letter.

ex.en: We have a small problem.

cards.note: Close to *küçük*, often for small, unimportant things: *ufak bir hata*. *Ufak tefek* = slight (of a person); odds and ends.

ex.en: I have to get up early tomorrow.

cards.note: Also an adjective: *erken bir saat*. The opposite is *geç*. *Erkenden* = early on, in good time.

ex.en: Bye, see you tomorrow!

cards.note: Said by the person leaving; the one who stays answers *güle güle*. To several people, or politely: *Hoşça kalın*.

ex.en: Our team consists of eleven people.

cards.note: *-DAn oluşmak* = to consist of. *Oluşturmak* = to form, to make up.

ex.en: There are seven days in a week.

cards.note: *Yedinci* = seventh. *Yedisinden yetmişine* = from seven to seventy: people of all ages.

ex.en: This man committed a crime.

cards.note: The e becomes i before `-(I)yor`: *işliyor*. *Suç işlemek* = to commit a crime; *işlenmiş* = processed, worked. Working at a job is *çalışmak*.

ex.en: There's a big tree in the garden.

cards.note: The ç becomes c before a vowel: *ağacı*. *Elma ağacı* = apple tree.

ex.en: It isn't easy to talk about your feelings.

cards.note: *Duygusal* = emotional, sentimental. *His* is close in meaning.

ex.en: The child threw a stone into the sea.

cards.note: A stone and stone as a material: *taş ev* (stone house). In games, a piece or a tile: *okey taşı*.

ex.en: Pack your things, we're leaving.

cards.note: An Arabic plural (of *şey*) used as a singular noun, so *eşyalar* is common too. *Ev eşyası* = household goods, furniture.

ex.en: I read a very interesting book.

cards.note: From *ilgi* (interest); *ilgilenmek* = to be interested (in: *-lA*).

ex.en: I sent you the file by email.

cards.note: A computer file, a paper folder, or a case file kept by the police or a hospital.

ex.en: We cleaned the house on the weekend.

cards.note: The e becomes i before `-(I)yor`: *temizliyor*. From *temiz* (clean); *temizlik* = cleaning.

ex.en: The bill, please!

cards.note: The p becomes b before a vowel: *hesabı*. *Banka hesabı* = bank account; *hesap makinesi* = calculator.

ex.en: Go a little further.

cards.note: The opposite is *geri*. *İleride* = up ahead; in the future. *İleri seviye* = advanced level.

ex.en: My goal this year is to learn Turkish.

cards.note: *Hedefine ulaşmak* = to reach your goal. *Amaç* is a purpose.

ex.en: Many of my friends live in Istanbul.

cards.note: Written as one word, and followed by a singular noun: *birçok insan*, *birçok kez*.

en: to have fun, to enjoy yourself

ex.en: We had a lot of fun at the party.

cards.note: *İyi eğlenceler!* = Have fun! With *-lA*, to make fun of: *Benimle eğlenme*. *Eğlenceli* = fun.

ex.en: My brother is a university student.

cards.note: From *öğrenmek* (to learn). *Öğrenci indirimi* = student discount.

ex.en: The hotel is very close to the city centre.

cards.note: *Şehir merkezi* = city centre, downtown; *alışveriş merkezi* = shopping mall.

ex.tr: Düğün için yeni bir elbise aldım.
ex.en: I bought a new dress for the wedding.

cards.note: A dress; in older or formal use, clothes in general. The everyday word for clothes is *kıyafet*.

ex.en: The food was really good.

cards.note: Before an adjective or an adverb: *gayet iyi* (perfectly fine). A bit more formal than *çok*.

ex.en: It's up to you.

cards.note: After the dative: *Sana bağlı* (It's up to you), *Havaya bağlı* (It depends on the weather). From *bağlamak*.

ex.en: My computer isn't working again.

cards.note: *Bilgi* (information) + *sayar* (counter). A laptop is a *dizüstü bilgisayar*.

ex.tr: Acil bir durum var, hemen gel!
ex.en: It's an emergency, come right away!

cards.note: *Acil servis* = emergency room; *acil durum* = emergency. Not *acele* (hurry).

ex.en: She looks just like her mother.

cards.note: Strengthens *gibi* or *benzemek*: *tıpkı senin gibi* (just like you). *Tıpatıp* = exactly alike.

ex.en: The poor cat is very hungry.

cards.note: **Poor** as in pitiful: *Zavallı çocuk!* = Poor kid! Without money is *fakir*.

ex.tr: Bir bardak soğuk su alabilir miyim?
ex.en: Can I have a glass of cold water?

cards.note: For things, the weather and distant people. For **I'm cold**, say *Üşüyorum*. *Soğuk algınlığı* = a cold.

ex.en: The dog attacked the child.

cards.note: The target takes the dative: *bize saldırdılar*. The noun is *saldırı* (attack).

ex.en: I bought a new pair of shoes.

cards.note: *Bir çift ayakkabı* = a pair of shoes; *genç bir çift* = a young couple. *Çift sayı* = even number; odd is *tek*.

ex.en: Your daughter is very clever.

cards.note: Close to *akıllı*. The noun is *zekâ* (intelligence), with â.

ex.en: Be honest with me.

cards.note: *Dürüst olmak gerekirse* = to be honest. *Dürüstlük* = honesty.

ex.en: The washing machine broke down again.

cards.note: *Çamaşır makinesi* = washing machine, *bulaşık makinesi* = dishwasher, *fotoğraf makinesi* = camera.

ex.en: I've seen this movie three times.

cards.note: Same as *kez* and *kere*: *ilk defa* (for the first time), *bir defa* (once).

ex.en: The wedding will be in June.

cards.note: The celebration; the marriage is *evlilik*, the civil ceremony *nikâh*.

en: to be confused, to get mixed up

ex.en: I'm not surprised at all.

cards.note: What surprises you takes the dative: *Buna şaşırdım*. Also to get confused: *Yolu şaşırdım* (I lost my way). *Şaşırtmak* = to surprise.

ex.en: Marriage isn't an easy thing.

cards.note: The k becomes ğ before a vowel: *evliliği*. From *evli* (married); *evlenmek* = to get married.

ex.en: The police found the bomb in time.

cards.note: Colloquially, *bomba gibi* = sensational, stunning: *bomba gibi bir haber*.

ex.tr: Akşam parkta bir dans gösterisi var.
ex.en: There's a dance show in the park this evening.

cards.note: From *göstermek* (to show). A protest march is a *gösteri yürüyüşü*.

ex.en: The police arrested the thief yesterday.

cards.note: The a becomes u before `-(I)yor`: *tutukluyor*. *Tutuklusunuz!* = You're under arrest! *Gözaltına almak* = to take into custody.

ex.en: We visited my grandfather on the weekend.

cards.note: *Ziyaret etmek* = to visit, with the accusative: a person or a place. *Ziyaretçi* = visitor.

ex.tr: Bir ile on arasında bir sayı seç.
ex.en: Pick a number between one and ten.

cards.note: A number in counting and math; a phone or house number is a *numara*.

ex.en: My aim is to speak Turkish.

cards.note: The ç becomes c before a vowel: *amacı*. *Amacıyla* = with the aim of.

ex.en: There are no customers in the shop.

cards.note: A shop's customer or a firm's client. *Müşteri hizmetleri* = customer service.

ex.en: He'll most likely come tomorrow.

cards.note: Front-vowel suffixes, because the l is a thin l: *ihtimali*, *ihtimalle*. *Büyük ihtimalle* = most likely.

ex.en: I broke my leg playing soccer.

cards.note: The k becomes ğ before a vowel: *bacağı*. The foot is *ayak*.

ex.en: The weather isn't bad at all.

cards.note: Mostly in *fena değil* (not bad). Colloquially also **really**: *Fena yoruldum* (I'm dead tired). Otherwise *kötü* is the usual word.

en: to set aside, to save (for someone)

ex.en: I saved you a piece of cake.

cards.note: To book: *masa ayırtmak* (to reserve a table). *Ayrılmak* = to leave; to split up.

ex.en: It's your choice.

cards.note: From *seçmek* (to choose). In the plural, often elections: *seçimler*.

ex.tr: Çay mı tercih edersin, kahve mi?
ex.en: Would you prefer tea or coffee?

cards.note: What you prefer takes the accusative, what you prefer it to the dative: *Çayı kahveye tercih ederim*. *Tercih* = preference, choice.

ex.en: Brush your teeth after eating.

cards.note: *Diş fırçası* = toothbrush, *diş macunu* = toothpaste, *dişçi* or *diş hekimi* = dentist.

ex.en: Dark clouds are coming.

cards.note: Mostly in set phrases and figurative uses (*kara haber*, bad news; *Karadeniz*, the Black Sea); the usual colour word is *siyah*. The noun *kara* means land.

en: to run into, to meet (by chance)

ex.tr: Dün markette eski bir arkadaşla karşılaştım.
ex.en: I ran into an old friend at the supermarket yesterday.

cards.note: Who or what you meet takes *-lA*: *bir sorunla karşılaşmak* (to come across a problem). A planned meeting is *buluşmak*.

ex.en: I have a bad feeling.

cards.note: The s doubles before a vowel: *hissi*. *Hissetmek* = to feel; *altıncı his* = sixth sense.

ex.en: This movie really moved me.

cards.note: The e becomes i before `-(I)yor`: *etkiliyor*. From *etki* (effect); *etkileyici* = impressive.

ex.en: There's a nice smell coming from the kitchen.

cards.note: *Kokmak* = to smell (of something): *Burası balık kokuyor*. *Kokulu* = scented.

ex.en: The apartment on the third floor is empty.

cards.note: A flat in an *apartman* (apartment building). Also a circle, and a government office: *vergi dairesi* (tax office).

ex.en: Is your mother better?

cards.note: *İyi* + `-lAş`. *Geçmiş olsun, çabuk iyileş!* = Get well soon!

ex.en: No problem, I'll take care of it.

cards.note: Same as *sorun*, the native word: *Problem yok* and *Sorun değil* both mean no problem.

ex.en: I woke up to the sound of birds this morning.

cards.note: *Kuş uçmaz kervan geçmez* = remote, in the middle of nowhere (literally, no bird flies and no caravan passes).

ex.en: Can you send me the photos?

cards.note: A colloquial *göndermek*. The a becomes u before `-(I)yor`: *yolluyor*.

ex.en: I got a good mark on the exam.

cards.note: *Not almak* = to take notes, or to get a mark; *not defteri* = notebook.

ex.en: She fought the illness for years.

cards.note: From *savaş* (war); the opponent takes *-lA*. A fistfight or a quarrel is *kavga*.

ex.en: Wear your red dress.

cards.note: Like other colour words, both a noun and an adjective: *kırmızı bir araba*. *Kırmızı ışık* = red light.

ex.en: The police gave me a ticket.

cards.note: *Ceza yemek* (colloquial) = to get a fine or a punishment; *park cezası* = parking ticket; *cezaevi* = prison.

ex.en: My daughter is studying medicine at university.

cards.note: *Üniversite okumak* = to study at university; *üniversiteli* = university student.

ex.en: We've already planned our vacation.

cards.note: The a becomes ı before `-(I)yor`: *planlıyor*. Also *plan yapmak*.

ex.tr: Babam otuz yıl memur olarak çalıştı.
ex.en: My father worked as a civil servant for thirty years.

cards.note: *Devlet memuru* = civil servant. *Memur bey* = officer, a polite way to address a police officer.

ex.en: History is my favourite subject.

cards.note: Both history and a date: *doğum tarihi* (date of birth), *tarih öncesi* (prehistory).

ex.en: He signalled to me with his hand.

cards.note: *İşaret etmek* = to point (at), to signal; *soru işareti* = question mark; *işaret dili* = sign language.

ex.en: Thanks a lot for your support.

cards.note: The k becomes ğ before a vowel: *desteği*. *Destek olmak* = to support, to stand by (dative): *Sana destek olurum*.

ex.tr: Türk yemeklerini, özellikle mantıyı çok severim.
ex.en: I love Turkish food, especially mantı.

cards.note: From *özel* (special) and *özellik* (feature).

ex.en: How many languages do you speak?

cards.note: Both the organ and a language: *yabancı dil* (foreign language), *ana dili* (mother tongue). Names of languages end in `-CA`: *Türkçe*.

ex.en: Ayşe will present her project tomorrow.

cards.note: Formal: to present a report or a show, to offer a service (*hizmet sunmak*). *Sunucu* = TV host, presenter.

ex.en: Suddenly the lights went out.

cards.note: Also **at once**: *hepsi birden* (all of them at once). *Aniden* is a synonym.

ex.en: The last scene of the movie was beautiful.

cards.note: *Sahneye çıkmak* = to go on stage.

ex.en: It snowed a lot last night.

cards.note: *Kar yağıyor* = it's snowing; *kardan adam* = snowman. Not *kâr* (profit), written with â.

ex.en: I'm busy right now, I'll call later.

cards.note: Front-vowel endings, because the l is a thin l (TDK): *meşgulüm*, *meşguldü*. *Hat meşgul* = the line is busy.

ex.en: We went to the game despite the rain.

cards.note: After the dative: *her şeye rağmen* (in spite of everything). With a clause: *-mAsInA rağmen*.

ex.en: This child has a talent for music.

cards.note: The k becomes ğ before a vowel: *yeteneği*. *Yetenekli* = talented.

ex.en: We're going the wrong way!

cards.note: *Ters yön* = the opposite direction. Also an aspect: *iyi yönleri* (its good sides).

ex.en: That kid is a little devil!

cards.note: Also said, half fondly, of a clever, mischievous person. *Şeytanın avukatı* = devil's advocate.

ex.en: A beer, please.

cards.note: *Fıçı bira* = draft beer. The classic Turkish spirit is *rakı*.

ex.en: I'm proud of you.

cards.note: *-lA gurur duymak* = to be proud of. *Gururlu* = proud; sometimes vain.

ex.en: What's the source of this news?

cards.note: The k becomes ğ before a vowel: *kaynağı*. *Kaynak suyu* = spring water. From *kaynamak* (to boil, to well up).

ex.en: Let's discuss this tomorrow.

cards.note: With *-lA*: *Annemle tartıştım* (I argued with my mom). The noun is *tartışma* (argument, debate).

ex.en: Vehicles can't enter this road.

cards.note: The ç becomes c before a vowel: *aracı*. Any vehicle, in news and on signs; also a tool: *araç gereç* (equipment).

ex.en: Nobody forced you.

cards.note: The a becomes u before `-(I)yor`: *zorluyor*. What someone is forced into takes the dative: *Beni gitmeye zorladı*.

ex.tr: Bu akşam maçı birlikte izleyelim mi?
ex.en: Shall we watch the game together tonight?

cards.note: The ç doesn't soften: *maçı*. *Maç kaç kaç?* = What's the score?

ex.en: The doctor suggested a new treatment.

cards.note: *Tedavi etmek* = to treat; *tedavi olmak* = to be treated, to get treatment.

ex.en: The boss fired him.

cards.note: *İşten kovulmak* = to be fired. Also to chase away: *Kediyi bahçeden kovdu*.

ex.en: Yes, madam, how can I help you?

cards.note: A polite way to address a woman; for a man, *beyefendi*. Written as one word.

ex.en: The concert was great!

cards.note: Colloquial, like *harika*. Also in *süpermarket*.

ex.en: The journey took eight hours.

cards.note: The k becomes ğ before a vowel: *yolculuğu*. From *yolcu* (passenger). *İyi yolculuklar!* = Have a good trip!

ex.en: Thank you very much for your invitation.

cards.note: *Davet etmek* = to invite, with the accusative. *Davetiye* = an invitation card; *davetli* = guest.

ex.en: The train leaves at nine.

cards.note: *Trenle gitmek* = to go by train; *tren istasyonu* = train station; *hızlı tren* = high-speed train.

ex.en: Is this neighbourhood safe at night?

cards.note: *Güven* (trust, security) + *-lI*. The opposite is *tehlikeli*. *Güvenlik* = security.

ex.en: The keys aren't in my pocket.

cards.note: The p becomes b before a vowel: *cebi*. *Cep telefonu* = cell phone; *cep harçlığı* = pocket money.

en: to come, to take, to have (polite; buyurun: please, here you are)

ex.en: Please, come in.

cards.note: Mostly in *Buyurun* (often said *Buyrun*): Here you are; Please come in; Yes, can I help you? Of a ruler in old texts, to command.

ex.en: The rain ruined all our plans.

cards.note: Written as one word, like *kaybetmek*. *Mahvolmak* = to be ruined: *Mahvoldum!* = I'm done for!
